 :Judgment:
This is a Petition filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of Boramma W/o Kempaiah in the Road Traffic Accident.
The petition is filed by the son of deceased Boramma.

2. The Brief averments of the Petition are as under:
That on 01.12.2022 at about 5.45 p.m., on Kunigal- Nelamangala Road, near Arepalya village, Thippasandra Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara, while Boramma (deceased) was standing on the extreme left-side of foot-path so as to cross the road, the Car bearing no.KA-13-P-9324 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the her.
As a result, she fell-down, sustained grievous-injuries and died on the spot.
3. That prior to the date of accident, Boramma was hale and healthy.
She was a vegetable vendor and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
4. That the accident is solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Respondent no.1 being the owner and Respondent no.2 being the insurer of the car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence this petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, Respondent no.1 & 2 appeared through their counsel and filed their objections to main petition.
6. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.1 has denied the negligent driving of the driver of car.
That C.S.Prasad-the driver of the car was driving it cautiously, but since Boramma suddenly came across, he was unable to control the car.
However, it is stated that the car was insured with respondent no.2.
Thus, Respondent no.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
7. In the Objection Statement, Respondent No.2- Insurance Company has denied the petition-averments in toto.
However the insurance in respect of the car bearing Reg. no.KA- 13-P-9324 has been admitted.
Thus, respondent no.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

8. On the rival pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
Chikkanna vs Deepak.N.H on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104427169/
2

entities.text: Chikkanna vs Deepak.N.H on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that he is the legal-representative of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioner proves that Boramma W/o Kempaiah died due to injuries sustained by her in an accident occurred on 01.12.2022 at about 5.45 p.m., on Kunigal-Nelamangala road, Thippasandra Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara, arising due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-9324?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
9. On his behalf, the petitioner has got himself examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 10.
On the other hand, Respondent no.1 & 2 have not led any evidence on their behalf.
10. Perused the pleadings and evidence on record.
Heard both-sides.

11. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4

: As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 12. Issue No.2: It is the case of the Petitioner that he is the son of deceased Boramma who died in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-13-P-9324.
13.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.

Respondent no.2 has however, admitted the issuance of Policy to the offending car bearing No.KA-13-P-9324.
14.
On his behalf, the petitioner has got himself examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to 10.

Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.8 are the true copy of FIR and Complaint, Charge sheet, Spot sketch & Spot Mahazar, IMV report, Reply to the Notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act and P.M. Report.
15.

A perusal of Exs.P.1 & 2 shows that on the complaint filed by the son of deceased Boramma, who is none other than the Petitioner, Kudur Police have registered the case against the driver of the car bearing no.KA-13-P-9324 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304A of IPC.
As per Exs.P.1 & 2, the accident occurred while Boramma was trying to cross the road.

The Spot Sketch and Mahazar at Exs.P.4 & 5 respectively, show that the accident has occurred almost on the edge of the Chikkanna vs Deepak.N.H on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104427169/
3 Main Road.
The fact that the accident has occurred almost on the edge of the road while Boramma was trying to cross the road, shows the negligence on the part of the car driver.

After investigation,
Police have filed the Charge-sheet at Ex.P.3 against the driver of car for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304A of IPC.
As per the the IMV report at Ex.P.6, the front-portion of the car is shown to have been damaged; and the accident is not due to any mechanical defect of the car.
Ex.P.6 is the Reply to the Notice under Section 133 of MV Act in which respondent no.1 has stated that one Prasad was driving the car at the time of accident.
Ex.P.8 is the Post Mortem Report which shows that cause of death as 'haemorrhage'.
Exs . P.9
& 10 are the notarized-copy of Aadhar cards of deceased Boramma and petitioner respectively.
16. Thus, the Spot Sketch at Ex.P.4 coupled with the Charge Sheet at Ex.P.3 proves the negligence of driver of the car.
On the contrary, Respondent no.1 & 2 have although denied the negligence on the part of the driver of car, they have not chosen to examine him, to rebut the evidence of petitioner.

Thus having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, oral & documentary evidence on record, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending-car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-9324, in which Boramma has been injured and sustained injuries and has later succumbed to the same.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'Affirmative'.
17. Issue No.1 and 3: Both these issues are taken-up together for discussion to avoid the repetition of the facts.

The petitioner has furnished the notarized-copy of Aadhar cards of himself and his deceased mother-Boramma as per Exs.P.9 & 10 respectively, in which the name of petitioner's father as well as the name of Boramma's Husband has been mentioned as 'Kempaiah', and their address as 'Arepalya' village.

Also, the petitioner is the one who has filed the complaint at Ex.P.2 stating that his mother - Boramma who was residing with him, was hit by the offending car bearing no.KA-13-P-9324 while she was trying to cross the road.
Ex.P.2 is first in point of time and cannot be disbelieved.
Thus Exs.P.9 & 10 coupled with Ex.P.2, prove the relationship of petitioner with that of deceased Boramma.
Moreover, there is no dispute regarding the relationship.
Thus it is proved that the petitioner is son and legal-representative of the deceased Boramma.
18. Next, as per the petition, the deceased was aged about 70 years.
However, as per the Aadhar Card at Ex.P.9, the date of birth of Boramma is shown as 01.01.1945, and she was aged about 77 years as on the date of accident in the year 2022.

The averment made in the complaint at Ex.P.2 that Boramma was residing with the petitioner, not only proves that the petitioner was not dependent on her but that she had no independent source of income, as contended.
19. Next as per the petition, Boramma was a vegetable vendor, earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But the petitioner has not produced any document to prove the occupation and income of Boramma.

20. Here, it would be apt to refer to the decision reported in: Civil Appeal No.2323 of 2025 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.444 of 2025) between Seema Rani & Ors Vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., &
Ors. Dated11.02.2025, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under:
Chikkanna vs Deepak.N.H on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104427169/
4 9.

entities.text: Seema Rani & Ors Vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "We have heard the learned counsel for the Appellants.
We are unable to agree with the view taken by the Tribunal on the dependents of the deceased.

This court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender & Ors, had expounded that major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal-representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The court went on to conclude that since the sons, in that case, were earning merely Rs.1,50,000/- per annum, they were largely dependent on the earnings of the deceased and were staying with her".

In the light of the above decision, the petitioner who is a married-son of deceased Boramma, is no doubt her 'legal- representative'; but in the absence of evidence (that the petitioner depended on the earnings of the deceased), he cannot be considered 'her dependent'.

Under the circumstances, the petitioner is though entitled for compensation, is not entitled for compensation under the Head 'Loss of Dependency'; and considering the age of deceased Boramma, no compensation under the Head 'Future Prospects' can be granted.

21. With this background, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled-to is discussed as under :
The petitioner who is the son of deceased, has lost the Love & affection of his mother.

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed that:
"Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family".

Here, it would be apt to the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others): wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: 'Loss of Estate' has to be compensated by awarding Rs.15,000/-, 'Loss of Consortium' should be Rs.40,000/- and 'Funeral Expenses' should be Rs.15,000/-".

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years".

In the light of the above decision, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head of 'Loss of Consortium' and Rupees 16,500/- towards 'Loss of Estate' and Rupees 16,500/- towards 'Funeral Expenses'.
22.
Next as per the petition, the Petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for shifting the dead body, for performing funeral & obsequies.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for some amount towards 'Transportation of Dead Body'.
An amount of Rs.10,000/- under this Head would be just and reasonable.

Chikkanna vs Deepak.N.H on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104427169/
5 23.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
1. Loss of Consortium Rs.44,000/-
2. Loss of Estate Rs.16,500/-
3. Funeral Expenses Rs.16,500/-
4. Transportation of Dead Body Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.87,000/-
Thus in all, the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.87,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
24. Regarding Liability : As already discussed above, the petitioner has proved that the accident is due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing no.KA-13-P-9324.
And, it is not in dispute that the Insurance Policy of the offending car issued by Respondent no.2-Insurance Company was valid as on the date of accident.
Therefore, Respondent no.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, Respondent no.2 being the insurer has to indemnify the insured, and it has to deposit the compensation amount with interest.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative' and Issue No.3 'Partly in the Affirmative".
25. Issue No.4 : From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.87,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.87,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Respondent no.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 30 days from the date of the Award.
The amount being meagre, on deposit of amount by respondent no.2, the entire amount is ordered to be released in favour of Petitioner by way of E- payment after proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:

3. Funeral Expenses Rs.16,500/-

Total Rs.87,000/-
Thus in all, the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.87,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
And, it is not in dispute that the Insurance Policy of the offending car issued by Respondent no.2-Insurance Company was valid as on the date of accident.
Therefore, Respondent no.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, Respondent no.2 being the insurer has to indemnify the insured, and it has to deposit the compensation amount with interest.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative' and Issue No.3 'Partly in the Affirmative".

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.87,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Respondent no.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 30 days from the date of the Award.
The amount being meagre, on deposit of amount by respondent no.2, the entire amount is ordered to be released in favour of Petitioner by way of E- payment after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
